regions.full_page: . Finally while Miss Gibson was sice in a Detroit hospital her girl-friend the other nurse - her "saintly friend" as she consi- dered, (a certain Miss Daily), died in New York. Just another knock for the girl-friend left to weep and to pray - - - of whom she was wont to speak as being a saint and on the help of whose prayers she still seems to have confidence. Having lingered at the Grave . Miss Gibson plucked a slip of an "immortal" (a little plant grow- ing on the grave), and simply put it in a little, round "vanity-box" perhaps two inches wide and a 1/2 of an inch deep, half saying to herself: "This will be my relique." Shortly afterwards she was packing her trunk to come West and without further ado, like tossed it into the trunk to take care of itself. Weeks afterwards she was looking for something else when the little "vanity-box" unexpectedly appeared. "O!", she thought, "Here is my relic!". Her emotion on finding it not only fresh and green but perfectly in bloom was un- speakably more than surprise. To me, when first I saw it and as of- ten as I saw it - which was quite occasionally for more than a year -- it was a "Blue-print from Heaven" and nothing less, of the insti- tution that she and Miss D. had been dreaming of and praying for . . . . "Get started . ", came to my lips the first thing following my astonishment. "Get started if necessary with a single patient in some old atic. and God Who loves tiny beginnings will know, as He always does know best, how and when to provide development." She did not have to start in such extremes. Her said little "miracullous blue-print" would seem to have carried her successfully at every turn; for she carried it with her everywhere and never hesitated to show it where appreciation for the supernatural might be expected. All this till Mercy Hall was well established and to stay. . . . Aye! "A really Catholic Hospital, with everything in detail and up to date . What a contrast after three years when Chapel and Altar were gone and no visits more to Jesus or reception of the Sac- taments! Still Miss G. was a Catholic. Still her Catholic pictures and statues were in the corredors and parlors. Stell, though she wore no "habit" she was keeping up reception of the Sacrament her- self. She had aged more than three years. Less than a quarter of an hour's visit was sufficiently revealent. Dr. Mcclellan was my hoste and chauffeur, and he had an operation scheduled that morning and we necessarily had to be brief. One could only wonder as to the cause or the purpose of it all. . But: "Who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor? ! !
